title: I Bought A $4,000 Dropshipping Course To Prove Its A Scam
summary: Teen dropshipper buys a four-thousand-dollar course to show it is ninety minutes of surface-level videos, and describes a mentorship that copied students' products.

assertions.quote: there's nothing in here that you cannot find for free in like an afternoon of searching
That video alone pulled something like 10 or some thousand people into his Discord and then he launched a course like all gurus do.
They'll flex income screenshots and and cars, and they'll tell you that they found some sort of secret system
He used that to compete directly against them.

verdicts.note: A documented allegation in this case; prevalence across mentorships is unknown.

assertions.quote: put that money into your first adsets to get your first sales and the losses will teach you much more than any PDF ever could

verdicts.note: Advice about learning method, not a measurable claim.

Across 580 comparisons, explicit instruction produced better learning than unassisted discovery (d = 0.38), and the authors conclude unassisted discovery does not benefit learners while feedback and worked examples do: trial and error alone is the weaker teacher, though the studies are classroom and lab tasks, not ad testing.
